title: Slow-cooker chicken with Italian peppers
subtitle: Pollo alla peperonata — chicken braised with sweet peppers and tomatoes
excerpt: Chicken thighs slow-cooked with red and yellow peppers, tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil. A southern Italian everyday dish that suits the slow cooker very well.
sourceNotes: Pollo alla peperonata is a traditional southern Italian dish of chicken braised with peppers in a tomato base. It is common in Campania, Basilicata, and Calabria, documented in Italian regional cookbooks throughout the 20th century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better the next day as the peppers and chicken absorb more of the tomato sauce.

content.text: Red and yellow peppers become very sweet after a long slow cook. They almost melt into the tomato sauce and create a thick, silky base for the chicken. Green peppers can be used, but they are more bitter and will not achieve the same sweetness.

Bone-in chicken thighs are the traditional choice here. They stay moist throughout the long cook and the bones add depth to the sauce. Boneless thighs also work if you prefer not to deal with bones at the table.
Serve over polenta, with crusty bread, or over pasta.

Add {{onion}} sliced onion, {{garlic}} of sliced garlic, {{pepper-red}} of sliced red pepper, and {{pepper-yellow}} of sliced yellow pepper to the slow cooker. Pour over {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree. Add {{oregano-dried}} of oregano and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and stir together.

Place {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thighs on top of the pepper and tomato base. Spoon some of the sauce over each piece. Add {{olives-kalamata}} of pitted kalamata olives if using. Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. Discard the bay leaves before serving.

rows.symptom: The peppers have dissolved into the sauce
rows.cause: Two very long hours will break peppers down completely.
rows.fix: This is actually desirable for this dish; it makes the sauce thicker and sweeter. Add a few fresh sliced roasted peppers at the table if you want texture.

rows.cause: The peppers and chicken both released liquid during cooking.
rows.fix: Remove the chicken and reduce the sauce on HIGH with the lid off for 20 minutes. Return the chicken and serve.

rows.cause: Three tablespoons of olive oil in a sealed pot with the chicken fat can create a very oily surface.
rows.fix: Skim the surface with a spoon before serving. Reduce the olive oil to 1 tablespoon next time.

rows.cause: The chicken sat on top of the sauce and did not cook in it.
rows.fix: Stir the shredded chicken through the sauce and cook for 10 more minutes so it absorbs the flavour. Next time push the chicken into the sauce rather than just laying it on top.

content.text: Peperonata, a soft stew of sweet peppers with tomatoes and olive oil, is one of the defining dishes of southern Italian cooking. It appears as a side dish and as a braising base for fish, pork, and chicken. The combination with chicken is widespread across Campania and Calabria. The slow cooker is very well suited to it because the peppers need a long cook to become soft and sweet.
